title.value: Block Contextual MDPs for Continual Learning
title.justification: The paper primarily discusses the Block Contextual MDP framework in the context of continual learning scenarios, focusing on how it addresses issues of nonstationarity and generalization in reinforcement learning.
title.quote: In this work, we propose to examine this continual reinforcement learning setting through the block contextual MDP (BC-MDP) framework, which enables us to relax the assumption of stationarity.

extractions.description: This paper introduces the Block Contextual MDP framework for addressing nonstationarity in continual reinforcement learning settings, enabling RL agents to generalize better across tasks. The framework incorporates smoothness properties to manage changing contexts in nonstationary environments, proposing an algorithm (ZeUS) for zero-shot adaptation and strong performance on several nonstationary environments.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning algorithms in the context of continual learning rather than eco-responsible topics related to climate change or sustainability. Hence, it doesn't fit into any of the predefined categories.
primary_category.quote: Our work is related to the Continual (or Lifelong) RL... nonstationarity can manifest in two ways... We focus on the ability to continually adapt (the policy) to unseen tasks.

secondary_categories.justification: The discussion is technical and relates to reinforcement learning, which doesn't align with eco-responsible categories.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose a representation learning algorithm to enable the use of the current RL algorithms (that rely on the prototypical MDP setting) in nonstationary environments.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper is centered around reinforcement learning concepts without direct relevance to eco-responsible sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose to model this more realistic, rich observation, nonstationary setting as a Block Contextual MDP (BC-MDP) ...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Similar to the main category, since the paper lacks eco-responsible context, it does not fit into any sub-category.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Real life settings present an additional challenge: we can not rely on access to (or knowledge of) an interpretable and compact (if not minimal) state space.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper introduces and discusses frameworks and algorithms specific to Reinforcement Learning in nonstationary environments, which isn't covered by the existing eco-responsible categories.
new_primary_category.quote: This framework challenges RL algorithms to handle both nonstationarity and rich observation settings ... and achieves strong performance on several nonstationary environments.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category is not directly applicable as the focus remains on reinforcement learning methodologies.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Consider a robot moving around in a warehouse and performing different tasks... We propose a method for learning a context space that satisfies the above property.
